AffectedStory.description:
One story a change affects: the capabilities it gains and loses, its backfill, whether
the upgrade is unavailable to it (it has history, and the change adds data-producing
capability), and its fingerprint before and after with its quality status after.
AffectedStory.title: AffectedStory

Backfill.description:
Whether the change needs a backfill for this story, and its estimate when it does. In M3
one is needed exactly when the upgrade is unavailable (no backfill exists until M7).
Backfill.title: Backfill

BackfillEstimate.description:
What re-deriving a story's data would take (FR-PROF-7): model calls, tokens, and the
duration in seconds with the calls made one after another.
BackfillEstimate.title: BackfillEstimate

BudgetBody.description:
The turn's model-call budget: its cap, the guardrail calls it reserved
(`guardrail_input`, `guardrail_output`) and the calls it made, which equal the entries of
`model_calls`.
BudgetBody.title: BudgetBody

BudgetOverride.description:
A request's own turn budget (NFR-PERF-6; #69), within the story's: ``max_calls`` (1 to
50, at most the story's ``max_model_calls_per_turn``) and ``deadline_s`` (seconds, at least
0.5 and at most the story's ``turn_deadline``); above either is 422 ``validation_error``.
BudgetOverride.title: BudgetOverride

CardImage.description: An image on a public card (FR-CAT-4; #105, #115): the media asset and its alt text.
CardImage.title: CardImage

CardRating.description:
The content rating on a public card (FR-RATE-3; #115): the rating, the version the shown
version was published under, and the rating's name.
CardRating.title: CardRating

ChainRef.description: A chain selector: the ``{turn, variant}`` of the chain's first (diverging) turn.
ChainRef.title: ChainRef

ChainRefBody.description: A chain: the ``{turn, variant}`` of its first (diverging) turn.
ChainRefBody.title: ChainRefBody

CharacterBody.description: A character as a read returns it; ``is_player`` marks a player character.
CharacterBody.title: CharacterBody

CharacterCard.description:
A catalog character's public card (``projection=card``, the default; FR-CAT-2,
FR-SCN-10): only what a player-facing client may show, never a definition field.
``version`` is the version shown; a draft read shows the draft with the latest published
version (``null`` before the first publish). Until #115, ``images`` and ``labels`` are empty
and ``content_rating`` is ``null``.
CharacterCard.title: CharacterCard

CharacterCreate.description:
``POST /catalog/characters``: the new entry's first draft — any of the draft's fields —
and, optionally, its ``owner``: an opaque principal, by default the requesting one, never
``system`` (FR-AUTH-5). Ownership confers no permission (FR-AUTH-8).

definition.personality: Patient, private and slow to trust.

examples.name: Mara Venn
examples.public_description: Keeps the light on Gull Rock.

definition.description: The private definition: returned only by the `full` projection.

owner.description: The entry's owner principal (default: the requesting principal; never `system`). Recorded, never interpreted.
owner.title: Owner

public_description.description: Free text for the public card; never seeded into a story.
public_description.title: Public Description

CharacterCreate.title: CharacterCreate

CharacterDefinition.description:
The private character definition (FR-CAT-2): who the character is. It is seeded into
every story the character joins and is otherwise returned only by the ``full`` projection.
Until #115 adds the other fields it holds ``personality``.
CharacterDefinition.title: CharacterDefinition

CharacterDefinitionPatch.description: The ``definition`` part of a draft patch: a key sets that field, ``null`` removes it.
CharacterDefinitionPatch.title: CharacterDefinitionPatch

CharacterDraftBody.description:
The draft after a create or save, in ``full``: ``draft_revision`` is the revision the
next save or publish must send; ``config_revision`` is the deployment's (unchanged).
CharacterDraftBody.title: CharacterDraftBody

CharacterFull.description:
A catalog character in full (``projection=full``; FR-SCN-10): the entry's envelope, the
public card's fields and the private ``definition``. ``draft_revision`` is present only on a
draft read (``?draft=true``): the revision the next save or publish must send.
``published_at`` is when ``version`` was published; ``companion_id`` names the character's
companion scenario (#116; ``null`` until then). ``owner_principal`` is the entry's owner
(FR-AUTH-5), recorded for listing and attribution only.
CharacterFull.title: CharacterFull

CharacterPatch.description:
``PATCH /catalog/characters/{id}``: a JSON merge patch (RFC 7386) over the draft — a key
sets that field, ``null`` removes it, and ``definition`` merges the same way — with the
``draft_revision`` it is based on (FR-CAT-3).

examples.public_description: Keeps the light on Gull Rock, and the logbook.

draft_revision.description: The draft revision this patch is based on; a stale one is 409 `draft_stale`.
draft_revision.title: Draft Revision

CharacterPatch.title: CharacterPatch

CharacterPublishedBody.description:
The version a publish made: its number, the draft's new ``draft_revision`` (the draft
still equals what was published), the entry's ``status``, when it was published, and the
validation ``report``.
CharacterPublishedBody.title: CharacterPublishedBody

CharacterRefBody.description: A character of the story: its id and name.
CharacterRefBody.title: CharacterRefBody

CharacterSpec.description: One character of a new story's cast. ``true_age`` is required (FR-CAT-12).
CharacterSpec.title: CharacterSpec

CharacterStatusBody.description:
The entry after archive or unarchive: its status, listing status, latest published
version and when it was published, its timestamps and its companion (``null`` until #116).
CharacterStatusBody.title: CharacterStatusBody

CharacterVersionBody.description: One published version: its number, when and by which principal it was published.
CharacterVersionBody.title: CharacterVersionBody

CharacterVersionsBody.description: Every published version of a catalog character, oldest first.
CharacterVersionsBody.title: CharacterVersionsBody

ConfigChangeItem.description:
One change: the revision it produced, the setting, its class, the old and new values
(secret-bearing values redacted), who made it and when.
ConfigChangeItem.title: ConfigChangeItem

ConfigChangesBody.description: A page of configuration changes, newest first, and the cursor to the next page.
ConfigChangesBody.title: ConfigChangesBody

ConfigClass.description: FR-CONC-15: how a setting's change reaches work in flight (see the module docstring).
ConfigClass.title: ConfigClass

ConfigReplacement.description:
``PUT /admin/model-config/{purpose}``: the purpose's own ``base_url``, ``model`` and
``params``, replaced in full. An omitted or ``null`` field inherits from ``default``
(``params`` per key). The API key is never part of this body (``extra=forbid``).
ConfigReplacement.title: ConfigReplacement

CreationRules.description:
What a story creator may change at creation: ``overridable`` dotted paths (a path names
the field and everything under it), and optional ``bounds`` for settings.
CreationRules.title: CreationRules

CreationSettings.description:
The settings a story is created with: the full ``StorySettings`` schema, unknown keys
refused. ``default_output_viewpoint`` names a character of the cast **by name** here; it is
stored as ``character:<id>``.

audit_retention_days.description:
How many days this story's audit records are kept before the ``retention_sweep`` deletes
them (FR-STORE-30; #71), 1 to 3650. ``None``: the deployment's ``audit_retention_days``
(default 90). Never affects story history. Prospective.
audit_retention_days.title: Audit Retention Days

default_output_viewpoint.description:
The viewpoint a read or respond falls back to when the request names none and has no
actor (FR-RESP-12): ``character:<id>``, never ``omniscient`` (#59 resolves it).
Interpretive: a Lite turn depends on it (#64).
default_output_viewpoint.title: Default Output Viewpoint

generation_settings.description: The story's override of the deployment's Lite generation defaults (FR-LITE-4).

guardrail_retry_budget.description:
How many times a turn whose reply broke an output policy is generated again before the
safe fallback is used (FR-GUARD-6; #68), over the whole turn; ``0`` goes straight to the
fallback. Prospective.
guardrail_retry_budget.title: Guardrail Retry Budget

lite_summary_chunk.description: The story's override of the transcript rows per level-0 summary segment (#72).
lite_summary_chunk.title: Lite Summary Chunk

lite_summary_max_tokens.description: The story's override of the rolling summary's token cap (#72).
lite_summary_max_tokens.title: Lite Summary Max Tokens

lite_window_messages.description:
The story's override of how many transcript rows a Lite prompt keeps verbatim before
older ones are summarised (#72).
lite_window_messages.title: Lite Window Messages

max_model_calls_per_turn.description:
The most model calls one turn may make (NFR-PERF-6; #69), 1 to 50. ``None``: the
deployment's default, else the Lite formula ``4 + 5 + G``. A cap below one generation plus
the story's model-assisted guardrail calls refuses every turn with 422
``budget_below_safety_minimum``. Prospective.
max_model_calls_per_turn.title: Max Model Calls Per Turn

regenerate_retry_budget.description:
How many times a turn whose read set was touched is regenerated before the call fails
with ``revision_conflict`` (FR-CONC-4c). Prospective.
regenerate_retry_budget.title: Regenerate Retry Budget

turn_concurrency.description:
Same-story turn concurrency (FR-CONC-5): ``reject`` refuses an overlapping turn as busy
(423 ``story_busy``), ``queue`` queues it in a per-story FIFO (#63). Stored in its own
``stories`` column. Prospective: a change applies to requests that arrive after it.
turn_concurrency.title: Turn Concurrency

turn_deadline.description:
A turn's wall-clock deadline in seconds (NFR-PERF-6; #69 adds the call budget). The turn
slot's lease is ``turn_deadline`` + 10 s, and a queued request waits at most this long
before it is answered 202. Prospective.
turn_deadline.title: Turn Deadline

turn_queue_max.description:
How many turns may wait behind the running one under ``queue`` (``None``: the
deployment's ``turn_queue_max``, default 5); one more is 423 ``story_busy``. Stored in its
own ``stories`` column. Prospective.
turn_queue_max.title: Turn Queue Max

CreationSettings.title: CreationSettings

CustomInstructionsBody.description: The story's custom instructions: standing guidance for the model, never facts.
CustomInstructionsBody.title: CustomInstructionsBody

CustomInstructionsRequest.description: The story's custom instructions, replacing the current text; ``""`` clears them.
CustomInstructionsRequest.title: CustomInstructionsRequest

CustomInstructionsWritten.description: The stored custom instructions after the edit (see ``PinnedMemoriesWritten``).
CustomInstructionsWritten.title: CustomInstructionsWritten

DegradationBody.description: A degradation step and its cause (`retry_budget`, `call_budget` or `deadline`).
DegradationBody.title: DegradationBody

DepictedSubject.description:
A subject an image or video depicts (FR-IMG-9): a story ``character``, a
``catalog_character`` or a ``persona``, by id. Stored as declared, unverified (the subject
may be created later), and indexed so that erasure finds the asset (FR-ADMIN-6).
DepictedSubject.title: DepictedSubject

DormantChainBody.description:
A dormant continuation (#66): turns ``from_turn``..``through_turn`` of the chain
``{from_turn, variant}``; ``POST /stories/{id}/swap`` makes it active.
``truncate_operation_id`` names the truncation whose tail it is, when ``untruncate`` would
undo that truncation.
DormantChainBody.title: DormantChainBody

EffectiveBudgetBody.description:
The budget the story's next turn plans with (#69): `max_model_calls_per_turn` and its
`source` (`story`, `deployment` or `formula`: `9 + G`), `turn_deadline`, the guardrail calls
G it reserves (`guardrail_input`, `guardrail_output`) and `minimum_required` (`1 + G`).
EffectiveBudgetBody.title: EffectiveBudgetBody

EffectiveConfig.description:
A story's effective configuration (FR-PROF-5,16): the profile and version it runs on,
every delivered setting at its effective value, and the configuration's fingerprint, the
capabilities it enables and its quality status (``uncertified`` in M3).

effective.description: An engine profile's settings, by capability module (FR-PROF-2).

EntityListRule.description:
Named entities; any whole-word mention matches, under the wordlist rules.

At story and character scope an empty ``names`` means "the story's characters": the names
are frozen into the rule when it is saved (the whole cast for a story policy, the character
itself for a character policy, #50). Every stored rule has names.
EntityListRule.title: EntityListRule

EntityType.description:
Every owned entity type (FR-AUTH-5), as ``entity_type`` columns and the registry in
``core.ownership`` name them.

EntryStatus.description:
A catalog entry's version status (FR-CAT-2; #103, #108): ``draft`` until its first
publish, then ``published``; ``archived`` entries still read but cannot be edited,
published or used to create a story until they are unarchived. Postgres enum

EntryStatus.title: EntryStatus

Error.description:
The one error envelope every surface uses (docs/02 §9): REST answers it with the error's
status; the library raises the matching ``EpistrelError``.

ForkRequest.description:

the chain's tip) along ``variant_chain`` (default the active chain) into a new story.

at_turn.description: The last turn to copy (0: only the story's setup).
at_turn.title: At Turn

owner.description: The fork's owner principal (default: the requesting principal, not the source's owner; never `system`). Recorded, never interpreted.

variant_chain.description: The chain to copy, `{turn, variant}` or `"turn:variant"` (default the active one); a dormant continuation becomes the fork's active history.

came from, its cast, and how many rows were copied per table.

ForkedFromBody.description:
The source story, the source revision the fork equals, the last turn copied, and the
chain followed (``null``: the active one).
ForkedFromBody.title: ForkedFromBody

GenerationMetadata.description:
How an image was generated (FR-CAT-4): the adapter, the model, the prompt and negative
prompt, the seed, the parameters (a JSON object of at most 8 KiB) and the ids of the
reference images. Stored and returned exactly as sent: a key that was not sent is not
returned.
GenerationMetadata.title: GenerationMetadata

GenerationSettings.description:
Generation settings at one layer: deployment Lite defaults, story override, or a

GenerationSettings.title: GenerationSettings

GuardrailBody.description:
The output gate's outcome: the released reply's violations (empty unless even the

GuardrailCallsBody.description:
Model calls the guardrails add: ``input`` per text checked (a character-scoped input
policy adds one when its character acts), ``output`` per output checkpoint.

GuardrailViolationBody.description: An output policy the released reply breaks.

What a change would do before it is applied (FR-PROF-7): the affected stories (ordered by
story id, at most 1,000; ``affected_count`` counts them all), the scenario recommendations
left unmet, the FR-VERIFY-15 guarantees lost, the fingerprints and quality status (at the top

One event to record. ``kind`` is free text here so that a kind M2 does not record is
refused with ``unsupported_event_kind`` rather than a generic validation error.

One result per event, in request order, the story's revision after the call, and what
the input gate spent: its ``model_calls`` (as a turn reports them) and ``elapsed_ms``.

MediaAsset.description:
A media asset's metadata (FR-MEDIA-1): its owner, kind, MIME type (sniffed from the
bytes), size, dimensions or duration (``null`` when no probe could read them), SHA-256
checksum, content rating and the rating's version it was uploaded under, alt text, caption,
generation metadata (as sent), source, state (``live``, or ``retired`` once deleted), the
subjects it depicts, who created it when, and, for a video, its poster's id (FR-MEDIA-3;
``null`` for an image).
MediaAsset.title: MediaAsset

MediaKind.description: What a media asset is: an ``image`` or a ``video`` (``image/*`` or ``video/*``).
MediaKind.title: MediaKind

MediaListBody.description:
A page of media assets, newest first; ``next_cursor`` fetches the next page (``null``
on the last).
MediaListBody.title: MediaListBody

MediaSource.description:
Where an asset came from: ``uploaded`` by the consumer, ``generated`` (M8), or
``extracted``: a video's poster taken from its first frame with ffmpeg (#107).
MediaSource.title: MediaSource

MediaState.description:
An asset's state: ``live``; ``retired`` once deleted (still served to what references
it); or ``candidate`` (an unattached catalog image, M8; private).
MediaState.title: MediaState

MediaUpload.description:
``POST /media``'s ``metadata`` part (FR-MEDIA-1): the asset's ``kind`` (which its bytes
must be), its content rating, optional alt text, caption and generation metadata, the
subjects it depicts (required: ``[]`` declares none), optionally its ``owner`` (default: the
requesting principal; never ``system``) and, for a video, its ``poster`` (FR-MEDIA-3).

RespondRequest.description:
``POST /stories/{id}/respond`` and ``Engine.respond``.

- ``actor_character_id``: whose input this is. Any cast member may act, a player's own
  character or not: who acts is the consumer's call (FR-AUTH-3).
- ``player_input``: the actor's ``say``/``do``; the turn's first beat. It is only ever the
  actor's own speech and action: there is no field for another character's words, and a
  ``say`` that quotes a render character is still the actor speaking (FR-AUTH-3 b).
- ``render_character_ids``: who answers, voiced in this order in one combined reply
  (FR-RESP-5, FR-LITE-5). Omitted: every cast member except the actor, or the actor when
  no one else is in the cast. The actor may be listed. An explicit empty list is refused,
  and duplicates are dropped.
- ``output_viewpoint``: ``character:<id>`` or ``omniscient``; default the actor.
- ``prompt_params``: ``length`` (``short``/``medium``/``long`` or a token cap),
  ``temperature`` and ``top_p``, for this request only (FR-RESP-3).
- ``scene_context``: non-authoritative; never stored or placed in a prompt.
- ``budget``: this turn's ``max_calls``/``deadline_s``, within the story's (#69).

info.description: Epistrel runs behind the consumer and must never be exposed to end users. It authenticates only the calling service, which sends one of the deployment's service credentials as `Authorization: Bearer <credential>`, and it holds no user roles, grants, or permissions: which end user may call which operation, act as which character, or request which output viewpoint is the consumer's decision, made before it calls. Its privacy guarantee is relative to the request: output is produced for the output viewpoint the request names, and Epistrel does not verify that the consumer was entitled to request that viewpoint, so Epistrel by itself does not stop a player from reaching another character's secrets. Every mutating call carries an opaque requesting principal in `X-Epistrel-Principal`, which Epistrel records for attribution and never interprets; use opaque IDs rather than names or email addresses, so recorded attribution identifies no one without your own records. Ownership and relations are labels the consumer defines; the engine never grants or withholds an action because of them. Ownership exists for listing, attribution and offboarding only.
info.title: Epistrel Engine

post.description:
Play one turn of a story. The request names the acting character (any character of the story; who acts as whom is your decision), what they say and/or do (`player_input`, the turn's first beat and only ever the actor's own words), who answers (`render_character_ids`: default every other character, voiced in the order given and composed into one message), the output viewpoint (`character:<id>` or `omniscient`; default the actor, then the story's default; echoed as `output_viewpoint`, and `beats` are produced for it), prompt parameters (`length`, `temperature`, `top_p`) and optional scene context.

The consumer does no retrieval or memory work: the prompt is assembled from the story's own records. Scene context is checked against the cast and then ignored: it is never stored and never placed in the model's context.

The response is the **finished** reply: under the `lite` profile it is generated in one model call (plus one `guardrail_check` per model-assisted output policy) and none of its claims is checked against the story's facts. Before it is released the reply is checked against the story's output policies: a reply that breaks one is generated again with the policy's message as a constraint, up to the story's `guardrail_retry_budget`, and then the character's safe fallback line is returned instead (`guardrail.fallback_used`, `degradation: ["safe_fallback"]`). Rejected drafts are audit records only. Several characters are voiced in one generation, and their knowledge is kept apart only by instructions in that shared prompt.

Every turn runs under a model-call budget and a deadline: the story's `max_model_calls_per_turn` (default `9 + G`, where G is one call per model-assisted input policy plus one per model-assisted output policy) and `turn_deadline`, or a smaller `budget: {max_calls, deadline_s}` in the request (above the story's is 422). A budget below one generation plus G is refused with 422 `budget_below_safety_minimum` (`details.minimum_required`) before any model call. The response reports `model_calls` (every attempt, failed ones included), `call_counts` by purpose, `elapsed_ms`, `budget` `{max_calls, reserved, used}` and each `degradation` step with its cause; a 503 carries `model_calls` and `elapsed_ms` in `details`. `queued_ms` is how long the turn waited in the story's turn queue (null when it never queued) and `first_call_offset_ms` the delay from the turn reaching the front (a queued turn starting, else the request arriving) to its first model call; `elapsed_ms` starts at that same moment.

Every response states the configuration the turn ran under (FR-PROF-16): its `fingerprint` (`sha256:` over the profile version, each purpose's model and every quality-relevant setting, prompt templates included), the `capabilities` it enables, and its `quality_status` (`uncertified` until a certification matches the fingerprint, which no M3 configuration can have).

Optional headers: `Idempotency-Key` (a retry returns the identical response) and `X-Epistrel-Expected-Revision` (a stale revision is refused with 409 and nothing written).

While another turn of the story runs, a story with `turn_concurrency: reject` (the default) answers 423 `story_busy` with `Retry-After`, and one with `queue` queues the turn and plays the queued turns in order, each after the previous one finished. The request waits for its queued turn up to the story's `turn_deadline`, then answers 202 `{operation_id, position}` with `Location: /operations/{id}` while the turn stays queued; `Prefer: respond-async` answers 202 at once. A retry under the same `Idempotency-Key` waits for the same turn. A full queue (`turn_queue_max`) is 423.

patch.description:
Change the story's settings with a JSON merge patch (RFC 7396): a key present sets that setting, `null` resets it to its default, and `generation_settings` merges the same way. `turn_concurrency` (`reject` | `queue`), `turn_queue_max` (1-50; `null`: the deployment's default, 5), `turn_deadline` (seconds), `max_model_calls_per_turn` (1-50; `null`: the deployment's default, else `9 + G`), `default_output_viewpoint` (`character:<id>` of the cast, never `omniscient`), `regenerate_retry_budget` (0-10), `guardrail_retry_budget` (0-5: regenerations after a reply breaks an output policy, before the safe fallback), `generation_settings`, `lite_window_messages`, `lite_summary_chunk` (2-200 rows per summary segment), `lite_summary_max_tokens` (the rolling summary's token cap) and `audit_retention_days` (1-3650; `null`: the deployment's). An unknown key is 422. `policies` (optional) upserts the story's own policies; an item that would relax a policy refuses the whole request with 422 `cannot_relax` before anything is written.

Every setting but `default_output_viewpoint` is prospective: it applies to requests that arrive after the write, never to a turn already running; `default_output_viewpoint` is interpretive (a turn in flight is checked against it when it commits). A write that changes something moves the story's `config_revision`.

Make the chain `to_variant_chain` (`{turn, variant}` of its first turn, as `GET /stories/{id}/variants` lists it) active: everything active after the turn where it parts from the active chain becomes `dormant`, and the chain's turns (and the work positioned on them) become `active`. Nothing is deleted; swapping back restores the exact prior state. Swapping to the active chain writes nothing (200, `operation_id` null). A chain that names no variant, or continues in more than one way, is 409 `unknown_chain` (with the `candidates` to choose from). Turns waiting in the story's queue fail with `timeline_changed`.

A control action: it bumps the story's timeline revision, and a turn generating while it commits is abandoned with 409 `timeline_changed`. `Idempotency-Key` and `X-Epistrel-Expected-Revision` are optional.

Reactivate exactly what the most recent truncation discarded (undo is last in, first out).
